label: text
text: Few Cabinets have received such a general blessing as that beatowed by the morning newspapers on M. Polneare's so-called "Ministry of the Franc." There is a general sigh of relief that a Government has at last been formed which looks like weathering the storm and solving the financial situation. Politics for the moment are forgotten except for a few minor criticisms, such as the inclusion of M. Herriot and M. Painleve in the Cabinet.

label: text
text:
The opinion, however, is in no way unanimous in forecasting the Government's financial programme.
The most startling intention in this connection is attributed to M. Polincare by the newspaper Le Journal (Democrat) that he intends to ask Parliament to agree to a prorogation for two years during which the Government will legislate by decree, the Premier's argument being that the franc cannot be cured overnight. It needs three or four years for a complete rest and relief from political strife.—Reuter.

label: text
text: The franc opened at 202 and improved to 200 to the £1.—Reuter. Closing Prices:

label: text
text: The French franc closed at 197% and the Belgian franc at 193½. Reuter.

label: text
text: Inspired quarters have lifted the veil of the Government's financial intentions sufficiently to indicate a two years' prorogation will not be adopted. On the contrary Parliament will probably sit until mid-August and vote on a comprehensive series of measures involving four to five milliards of increased taxation direct and indirect in which succession duties figure largely.

label: text
text: The Government has ruled out the capital Levy, the moratorium, and fresh inflation, and will honour debt agreements, though it will seek a modification of the Washington Convention, with a view to the insertion of transfer and safeguard clauses. Finally, the stabilisation of the franc will be left until the exchange position is remedied.—Reuter.

label: text
text:
Shanghai, July 24.
Several hundred workers who went on strike at a Japanese cotton mill on June 24, agreed to return to work to-day.

label: text
text: The list of conditions presented to them by the Japanese management, which has been accepted, shows that the mills have won a distinct victory.

label: text
text: Super-unruly workers, "locked out" during the past four weeks have caused considerable disturbance in labour circles.

label: text
text: The acceptance by the workers of the management's demands is undoubtedly the result of the workers being starved out.—Reuter.

label: text
text: [A cable from Shanghai, dated June 24, stated:—There has been considerable unrest and agitation in local industrial circles, and lightning strike has been called in a Japanese cotton mill. Six hundred, downed tools, protesting against the arrest of a mill detective. The strikers set fire to the cotton, and when the brigade arrived they were attacked by the strikers with bricks, spanners and other heavy missiles. The Police drew their revolvers, but there was no firing. Twelve arrests were made, and the situation is considered most serious.]

text: Admiral Bristol has returned from Angora, where he renewed the Turbo-American Provisional Treaty of Commerce until February 20, 1927. Reuter's American Service

New York, July 24.
Some of the Mexican schools intend to close down and reopen across the American border, where the children will be religiously instructed unhampered.—Reuter.

label: text
text: A. pastoral letter has been signed by all the Archbishop's proposing, as a protest against the religious regulations, which will be enforced on August 1, that all Catholic services be suspended and priests withdrawn from the churches on July 31.—Reuter.

label: text
text: An earlier New York enable stated:—The newspapers are considerably preoccupied with the troubles of Roman Catholics in Mexico, where the new law regulating religion becomes effective on August 1. A Mexico City despatch stats that President Calles has issued a proclamation prohibiting religious instruction and worship in all schools and forbidding any cleric to direct a private school. Telegrams from Nogales and Arizona report that the Archbishop of Mexico and the Bishop of Tobasco have been arrested on a charge of violating the law by calling on Catholics to exert economic pressure on the Government with the object of obtaining an amendment of the church laws.

label: text
text: Sir Austen Chamberlain, Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs, and Baron Rubido-Zicby, Hungarian Minister in London, yesterday signed the text of the British-Hungarian Treaty of Commerce and protocol providing for continuance of a commercial status quo between the two countries until the new treaty has been duly ratified by the high contracting parties. The basis of the treaty is reciprocal freedom of commerce and navigation and mutual and absolute most favoured nation treatment between the two countries.—British Wireless Service.

text: BRITAIN GETS LAND AND AMERICA THE DOLLARS.

label: text
text: Senator Borah, in a statement, says European critics of America in connection with war debts should remember that people living in glass-houses should not throw stones.

label: text
text: He refers. to the "territorial acquisitions to Great Britain at the peace table," and adds that out of four million square miles to be divided, Britain secured 3,000,000 and France, 800,000.

label: text
text: America, true to her ideals, accepted nothing.—Reuter's American Service.

label: text
text: There are reports to the effect that General Yen Hsi-shan and the Kuominchun have reached an armistice. This is officially denied in Peking.

label: text
text:
Nanking telegrams report that General Sun Chuan-fang is now inclined to attack General Tang Seng-chi as he does not wish a material weakening of Marshal Wu Pel-fu in the Yangtze district.—
Reuter.

label: text
text: The vernacular papers state that Sun Chuan-fang has issued a circular telegram, which has been forwarded to the Cabinet and the provinces, advocating the cessation of the present hostilities.—Reuter.

label: text
text: An unfavourable impression has been created on the Stock Exchange by the announcement of the Directors of Marconi's Wireless Telegraph Company that no dividend is possible on the ordinary shares in respect of the working for the year 1925, although the results of the trading show a profit.

label: text
text: The Board states that a further revision of the values of certain of the Company's interests in the associated and other Companies will become necessary owing to continued depreciation.

label: text
text: Meantime the annual meeting of shareholders has been postponed sine die.

label: text
text: The Directors state that they intend to secure profits on future operations and that henceforth these will not be diminished by losses incurred owing to possible future depreciation of investments.

label: text
text: The Company's shares have fallen—substantially during the past days and are now quoted at 17s. 6d.—the lowest for ten years.—Reuter.

label: text
text: It is announced that the Treasury will not continue the argument as to whether the loans to Great Britain in war time were for commercial purposes.

label: text
text: Mr. Garrard B. Winston, Acting Secretary to the Treasury, reiterates that this is so: — Reuter's American Service.

label: text
text: A meeting of the Tariff delegates was to take place yesterday afternoon to discuss the continuation of the Conference, the main question being the length of the Summer recess.—Reuter.

text: Mr. Alan Cobham has arrived here.—Reuter.
